title: Product-preserving exact functors preserve the canonical derived-limit mate
statement: Let T and S be schemes, and let R and R′ be arbitrary commutative ring sheaves on their small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let F:Mod(R)→Mod(R′) be additive and preserve finite limits and finite colimits [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Equip its postcomposition functor on strict natural-number towers with finite-limit and finite-colimit preservation. Suppose the canonical product comparison F(∏ₙ Mₙ)→∏ₙ F(Mₙ) is invertible for every sequence M. For the actual total right-derived inverse-limit functors [prop-weil-pbc-rlim-functoriality] and the exact derived constant-tower functors, the mate of the localized identity-component constant-tower square is an isomorphism Rlim_R ⋙ D(F) ≅ D(F^Tow) ⋙ Rlim_R′. This specifies the particular mate for the canonical constant/limit adjunctions, not just an isomorphism of its endpoints; no boundedness or Noetherian assumptions occur.

source.place: Tags 0940 and 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok: limit inclusion into the two-product Roos model. The canonical mate identification is the projection/universal-unit calculation of the item proof step 5.

proof.text: Use exact countable products on both pro-etale module categories. Transport each actual right-derived strict inverse limit from homotopy categories to complex localization and across the canonical ordinary-limit model isomorphism. Choose the existing normalized Roos corner models, and use preservation of products to obtain the isomorphism on the two signed coordinates, descending to lambda.

The Roos inclusion normalization gives the comparison equation on every complex. Cancel the ordinary-limit model isomorphisms and check every limit projection to identify its ordinary map with preservesLimitNatIso. The ordinary constant-tower mate has these same projections.

The exact/derived mate factorization for the fixed constant-limit adjunctions intertwines the same universal right-derived units and ordinary comparison. Extensionality for the right-derived composite identifies the descended lambda with this specified mate. Invertibility follows because lambda is an isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0941: specialize the existing proved normalized Roos comparison and identify the mate by universal-unit uniqueness. Reuses the general calculation in CompletedOpenEndpointLimitTransport without importing that descendant.

theorem productPreservingDerivedLimitMate_isIso {T S : Scheme.{t}}
    {R : Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) CommRingCat.{t + 1}}
    {R' : Sheaf (ProEt.topology S) CommRingCat.{t + 1}}
    (F : reductionModules T R ⥤ reductionModules S R') [F.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteColimits F]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits ((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj F)]
    [PreservesFiniteColimits ((Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ _ _).obj F)]
    (hphi : ∀ N : ℕ → reductionModules T R, IsIso (piComparison F N)) :
    IsIso (mateEquiv
      (constLimAdj : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : reductionModules T R ⥤ _) ⊣
        completedTowerLimit T R).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
      (constLimAdj : (Functor.const ℕᵒᵖ : reductionModules S R' ⥤ _) ⊣
        completedTowerLimit S R').mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction
      (TwoSquare.mk _ _ _ _
        (Functor.mapDerivedCategorySquareIso (Functor.compConstIso ℕᵒᵖ F)).hom)).natTrans
